result.architecture_summary: The target architecture has a sound core—versioned canon, bounded workers, deterministic readiness, isolated Git work, evidence-based validation, and merge-gated completion—but the implemented system is mostly a one-time planning bootstrap. It can identify seven nominally ready tasks, yet cannot safely claim, execute, revise, complete, supersede, or reconcile them after the GDD changes. The frozen repository therefore has strong bootstrap auditability but no coherent ongoing workflow state machine.
result.verdict_reason: Do not discard the bounded-worker and evidence-validation ideas, but reject the current milestone order and durable-state design. The most important post-bootstrap transitions are absent, while the repository has already invested heavily in global reconciliation, multi-model verification, recovery, and copied audit output. This will not materially accelerate game development until one real feature can travel through planning, execution, Unity validation, merge, and durable completion.
strong_decisions: The LLM does not own durable state or the continuous loop.
Integrated `main` is correctly treated as authority for what implementation exists.
Workers are bounded to one contract and cannot self-declare completion.
Dependency readiness is deterministic rather than reconstructed by an LLM.
Unity/runtime evidence can override a static evaluator pass.
Single-worker reliability is required before parallelism.
The bootstrap approval manifest binds exact immutable artifacts by hash, and publication places the completion marker last.
Reconciliation verification caught 21 material findings in the initial candidate before human approval.
structural_flaws: Post-bootstrap reconciliation is a stub. When `Tasks/*.yaml` exists, it returns `taskcontrol_diff_required` but emits empty `proposed_changes` and `conflicts`; the promised diff/apply workflow does not exist.
`taskcontrol` has only validate/list/show/ready/graph. There is no claim, transition, block, complete, supersede, reconcile-diff, or transactional apply command.
The durable lifecycle has only `open` and `complete`. It cannot represent claimed, validating, needs-human, invalidated-by-canon, needs-replan, canceled, superseded, or abandoned work.
Completion is not causally linked to a merge SHA or validation evidence. The smoke test demonstrates completion by directly editing `status` to `complete`.

The Git ordering is unresolved: implementation must be merged before a task is complete, but the task status cannot truthfully be marked complete on the pre-merge ticket branch. A post-merge update needs its own idempotent transaction and crash reconciliation.
Tasks copy large amounts of GDD prose instead of referencing stable, versioned requirement identities. This creates stale duplicated canon.

Some nominally executable contracts are internally ambiguous. NSC-019 is `single_agent` and `concrete` while admitting that Input Actions ownership is unresolved. NSC-003 requires integration validation against consumers that do not yet exist.
Completed NSC-023 retains a future integration validation obligation, but there is no revalidation lifecycle or downstream compliance record.

The GDD mixes game design with development architecture, token budgets, locks, agent roles, and branch policy. Those policies are then duplicated in ADRs and `PROJECT_REQUIREMENTS.yaml`, causing authority feedback loops.

`outputs/current/STATUS.md` still says the graph awaits human approval and seeding even though Milestone 1 is complete. `CURRENT_STATE.md` also says Assignment 7 is not implemented despite a substantial checked-in implementation. The repository already demonstrates duplicated-current-state drift.
observed_failure_solutions: Assignment 6 runtime feedback solved real camera failures missed by repeated static evaluator passes: wrong facing, missing follow behavior, and incorrect framing.
The no-op progress guard solved an observed Refiner false-success where the agent reported `implemented` without changing `Assets/`.
Bounded repair attempts and the circuit breaker prevent the observed GER repair loop from continuing indefinitely.
Append-only runtime feedback preserves the two real human Play Mode failure reports.
Raw-result preservation, retry handling, interrupted-refinement resume, identity-order repair, and evidence-boundary fixes address real failures encountered while running the reconciliation system.
Independent reconciliation verification found and repaired semantic omissions, dependency problems, evidence problems, and execution-sizing findings before bootstrap.
Atomic staging/reload validation and last-marker publication address partial initial graph publication, although hard-interruption recovery remains manual.
The frozen commit’s Git configuration addresses an actual Windows-host/Linux-container clean-status mismatch.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Claims, leases, resource collision scheduling, worktrees, GitHub synchronization, and merge queues mostly protect future parallel execution; no production supervisor currently exercises them.
Artifact Authority and Artifact GER may eventually prevent unauthorized design invention, but the current graph contains zero artifact records and no real feature has needed this path.
Progressive Decomposition is plausible for distant content work, but building it before one ready task ships would protect a hypothetical planning problem while execution remains impossible.
Incremental repository scanning and broad context caching are speculative optimizations; the current game is small enough for targeted file inspection.
The multi-stream arbitration and repair machinery is much larger than necessary for ordinary feature delivery. Much of it handles failure modes created by the reconciliation system itself.
Broad GitHub Projects mirroring, automatic backlog replenishment, parallel workers, and merge queues have no near-term proof of value.
overengineering: After the Assignment 6 gameplay commit, approximately 130,935 lines across 379 files were added while no later commit touched `Assets/`. Generated audit artifacts dominate that growth, but they still impose repository and cognitive cost.
Pipeline/docs/tasks total roughly 97,425 lines versus about 3,819 lines under `Assets/NoSafeCircle`.

A single 37-record bootstrap produced parallel reconciliation workers, multiple verification passes, stream repairs, arbitration, layout migration, recovery utilities, duplicated current views, and many checked-in patch-installer directories.
The project built extensive semantic assurance around choosing work before implementing the minimal mechanism that performs and closes work.
Several full candidate, raw candidate, Markdown rendering, verifier, refinement, and mutable-current copies preserve nearly identical information.
The proposed Milestone 2 bundles RAG, scanner, context building, two decomposition modes, artifact authority, generation, GER, and promotion. That is several milestones disguised as one.
missing_components: A single authoritative mutable workflow ledger with explicit legal transitions and compare-and-set semantics.
Transactional post-bootstrap task creation, revision, supersession, dependency editing, and completion.
Stable requirement IDs plus GDD revision/content hashes and an impact map from requirements to tasks, tests, artifacts, and implementation.
A freshness gate that refuses to use RAG data built from a different GDD revision.
A one-ticket controller with an idempotency key, base SHA, task-contract hash, attempt identity, and restart reconciliation.
Merge-linked completion metadata containing merge SHA and required validation evidence.
A real Unity batch adapter that captures compilation, EditMode, and PlayMode results in machine-readable form on a Unity-capable machine.
Disposition semantics for blocked, needs-human, failed, canceled, superseded, and canon-invalidated work.
A policy for in-progress and completed work affected by a GDD revision.
A human-decision queue with persisted answers and their canon/architecture scope.
A defined one-way GitHub projection or a deliberate choice to make GitHub the operational authority; the current future mirror has no conflict protocol.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary authorities are: versioned game-design canon, integrated `main` for implementation, one work-contract/requirement store, one mutable run/lifecycle ledger, immutable validation evidence, and explicit human decisions.
The current repository duplicates GDD rules across the Markdown GDD, stale RAG chunks, reconciliation candidates, task acceptance criteria, project requirements, and evaluator prompts.
Development-process policy is duplicated between the GDD, ADRs, milestone documents, and `PROJECT_REQUIREMENTS.yaml`. It should be removed from gameplay canon and owned by pipeline policy/ADRs.

`Tasks/*.yaml` is called the operational authority while GitHub is planned to own transient status, but no ordering or reconciliation rule handles disagreement, network failure, crash recovery, or a merged PR with an open task.
The mutable `outputs/current/` view is explicitly non-authoritative but presents itself as the current answer and is already stale. It should be generated on demand or removed.

The validator requires IDs to remain the contiguous range `1..task_count` and forbids dropping below the bootstrap count. This biases state toward permanent accumulation without explicit tombstone or supersession semantics.

The initial publisher is detectable but not fully recoverable after a hard crash between multiple `os.replace` operations: the marker is absent, readers reject the graph, and rerunning bootstrap refuses the already-published task files.
Resource groups duplicate membership in both every task and a global metadata file, requiring coordinated mutation without an implemented transactional writer.
gdd_iteration_concerns: This is already an observed problem, not a future concern. The GDD received eleven commits over August 19–21 and changed material mechanics such as held door interaction versus click-to-approach and manual versus automatic locking.

The checked-in RAG database still identifies the GDD as revised 2026-07-30 and retrieves obsolete rules such as `Hold for five seconds` and manual close/lock. The current GDD is revised 2026-08-21 and says no sustained hold plus automatic lock.
All 20 retrieval tests pass despite this contradiction because they test ranking, identifiers, and source-path existence—not source freshness or semantic equality.

The current Unity implementation and PlayMode tests still encode release-cancels-held-interaction behavior invalidated by the newer GDD. This demonstrates that passing tests may certify obsolete canon.
Current tasks have no GDD revision/hash. A task can remain ready while its copied acceptance criteria silently diverge from canon.
A later full reconciliation cannot fix this today: with the graph present, the implemented delta builder emits no actual live-graph changes.

For planned work, a material canon change should move affected work to `needs_replan` and remove it from readiness. For active work, it should invalidate the contract and require an explicit continue/abort decision. For validating work, it should invalidate prior semantic validation. For completed work, historical completion should remain immutable while a new revalidation/remediation item records whether current canon is still satisfied.
RAG indexes and context packs must be content-addressed by GDD revision and fail closed on mismatch. Cache invalidation cannot remain a two-line future note.
Synchronization with evolving canon should be incremental requirement-impact analysis, not repeated global roadmap reconstruction.
result.throughput_assessment: The present system is unlikely to turn weeks into days. It proves that a large initial plan can be audited and queried, but not that gameplay can be delivered repeatedly. If forbidden to build infrastructure for one slice, an agent could manually implement NSC-003 from its task file, but the machinery would first risk supplying stale RAG canon and would later have no authoritative way to claim the task, resume after interruption, validate it in Unity, associate evidence with a merge, or mark it complete. The first hard workflow break is the missing run/completion transaction; the first correctness break is stale canon retrieval. The absence of any `Assets/` commit after Assignment 6 while roughly 130k lines were added elsewhere is strong negative throughput evidence.
human_intervention_points: Approve material mechanics, scope, architecture, and interpretations where the iterative GDD is intentionally undecided.
Review the requirement-impact report after a material GDD change, especially effects on active or completed features.
Perform Unity editor inspection of scenes, prefabs, serialized references, imports, lighting, and visual composition.
Playtest game feel, readability, balance, timing, and first-time-player comprehension.
Review and merge changes until the automated validation path demonstrates an acceptably low false-pass rate.
Resolve Unity scene/prefab/shared-asset conflicts and decide the fate of non-canonical stub scenes.
Approve generated design/content artifacts when a real feature eventually needs them.
Supply credentials, Unity licensing/environment access, and external assets without committing secrets.

next_slice.title: Ship NSC-003 through one durable delivery transaction
next_slice.why: NSC-003 is visible gameplay, unlocks door interaction and two spells, and will expose whether the claimed task boundary and validation model are truthful. This slice should pause generic Milestone 2 work and implement only enough workflow to take one real feature from selected to merged and durably complete.
deliverables: Before execution, repair the NSC-003 contract: bind it to the current GDD hash, remove duplicated acceptance criteria, and move future consumer-integration validation to the relevant downstream tasks.
Implement mouse click/hold movement, shared gameplay-plane pointer projection, restriction/reset/suspend interfaces, Input Actions integration, scene-builder wiring, and focused tests.
Use direct current GDD sections and targeted repository files; do not use the stale RAG index or build a generic scanner.
Create one restartable attempt record containing task ID, contract hash, GDD hash, base SHA, branch, attempt ID, state transitions, commits, and evidence paths.
Run Unity compilation plus focused EditMode/PlayMode tests on a Unity-capable machine and record a human Play Mode checklist/result for movement feel and pointer correctness.
Merge through the normal review path, then perform an idempotent compare-and-set completion transition that records the merge SHA and evidence references.
Restart the controller once during the attempt to prove it resumes rather than duplicating the branch, run, or implementation.
next_slice.proof_of_value: From a clean restart, one NSC-003 attempt resumes without duplicate work, produces playable mouse movement on the canonical scene, passes recorded Unity validation, merges once, and changes the durable materialized state exactly once so NSC-019 becomes ready. That is the first credible evidence of development leverage.

do_not_build_yet: Generic RAG service or incremental project-state cache beyond a GDD freshness check.
Artifact Authority, artifact generation, or Artifact GER until a real blocked feature needs new approved design.
Another full reconciliation or multi-model verification run.
GitHub Projects bidirectional synchronization; first choose one operational authority.
Parallel workers, merge queue, or generalized resource leases.
Generic evaluator-profile framework beyond what NSC-003 actually needs.
More architecture-review orchestration or checked-in patch-installer variants.

alternative_architecture.description: Replace the reconciliation-first roadmap platform with a thin, change-driven feature-delivery controller. State: keep the GDD and a small stable requirement registry in Git; make task-contract revisions immutable and bind each to requirement/GDD hashes; keep exactly one mutable workflow ledger with explicit states (`planned`, `ready`, `running`, `validating`, `review`, `blocked`, `needs_human`, `done`, `superseded`, `needs_replan`). Treat GitHub as a one-way projection unless deliberately selected as that ledger. Planning: create or revise only near-frontier vertical slices from requirement changes and current repository evidence; no global multi-model reconciliation during normal progress. Execution: the controller performs a compare-and-set claim, creates/reuses a deterministic branch/worktree, records base SHA and attempt identity, then launches one bounded coding worker. Validation: collect Git scope checks, compilation, Unity EditMode/PlayMode XML, task-specific semantic review, and explicit human gates into one evidence manifest. Completion: a merged PR/merge SHA is implementation authority; recovery detects merged-but-unclosed tasks and records completion exactly once. Recovery: replay the ledger, inspect branch/worktree/PR/merge state, and resume or escalate without trusting worker output. Unity integration: run a small machine-local Unity CLI adapter and retain human Play Mode/editor checks for visual or interaction claims. GDD evolution: compute requirement-level changes, mark linked planned/active work as impacted, invalidate stale contexts/evidence, and create remediation/revalidation work for previously completed implementations without rewriting history.
alternative_architecture.why_better: It preserves the sound bounded-worker, Git isolation, deterministic computation, runtime evidence, and human-authority principles while removing the global reconciliation bottleneck and duplicated operational stores. It makes canon change a normal causal event, defines recoverable legal transitions, and directs almost every new line of infrastructure toward shipping the next playable slice.

evidence.observation: The live-graph branch explicitly defers comparison to future taskcontrol logic and returns empty `proposed_changes` and `conflicts`.
The parser exposes only validate, list, show, ready, and graph; no mutation or lifecycle operations exist.
The only demonstrated completion transition directly edits a task file’s status and contains no merge or evidence precondition.
Persistent IDs must remain one contiguous range from 1 through current task count, with no supersession/tombstone semantics.
A nominally ready task includes validation against consumers that do not exist yet and contains no GDD revision or completion-evidence fields.
The task is marked concrete/single-agent while line 104 says Input Actions ownership remains unresolved.
The only completed implementation still has a future visual-foundation integration validation requirement but no revalidation lifecycle.
The index identifies a 2026-07-30 GDD and contains obsolete held-interaction/manual-lock rules at lines 397 and 866.
Current canon instead requires click-to-approach, automatic timing without a sustained hold, and automatic close-and-lock after crossing.
Retrieval tests validate chunk count, unique IDs, ranking, and source-path existence but do not bind the index to current GDD content; all 20 tests passed during review despite semantic staleness.
Current PlayMode tests still require releasing interaction to cancel, reflecting the obsolete held-input design.
Static evaluation passed twice while the camera remained unusable; human Unity testing and structured runtime feedback drove the successful repairs.
The project observed a no-op Refiner false-success and added a progress guard that consumed retry budget.
Bootstrap publication is carefully staged and marker-last, but consists of several filesystem replacements with only best-effort rollback.
The mutable current view still says human approval and graph seeding are pending even though `Tasks/` and the completed bootstrap marker exist.
The document says Assignment 7 is not implemented, while `Assignment7StyleGuide/style_pipeline.py` and successful outputs are present.
Approximately 130,935 lines across 379 files were added after Assignment 6, while no subsequent commit touched `Assets/`.
Eleven GDD revisions landed between August 19 and August 21, demonstrating that canon is already a rapidly moving target.

result.biggest_uncertainty: Unity runtime execution and GitHub operational state may exist outside the frozen repository. Nothing in commit `aacbd57e10c9b4e9e40ef356935877527bc2411e` demonstrates such an external supervisor, lifecycle ledger, CI adapter, or synchronization protocol.
